preview: An interview experience detailing a coding round and three interview rounds including technical, DSA, OS questions, and final selection.
content: Coding Round: It was held in college on 20 Jan,17 for duration of 90 minutes. There were 3 coding questions. 1st Problem: You have 2 wheeled vehicles, and 4 wheeled vehicles. You are given a number ‘n’ as input, in how many ways you can collect ‘n’ number of wheels using those vehicles. So for n = 8 Ans = 3 Since you can collect it as (4, 4) or (4, 2, 2) or (2, 2, 2, 2). For odd ‘n’ answer is 0. 2nd Problem: Beautiful String There are 3 kinds of characters, [a-zA-z] letters, [0-9] numbers, and some special symbols [/\*]. Beautiful string is the string of the form: Starting with a letter, then there are 0 or more numbers, then there is a ‘/’, after that one or more letter or number, then a ‘\’, lastly one or more letter or number or ‘*’. (I don’t remember exact expression but it was of this form only) You are given a string as input, print number of substring which follows the Beautiful String expression. Input: a4/v1\v*3 Output: 6 Substrings: a4/v1\v, a4/v1\v*, a4/v1\v*3, 4/v1\v, 4/v1\v*, 4/v1\v*3 3rd Problem: You are given an array of integers (non-descending) and one number ‘n’. From the given array take any ‘n’ elements to make a new array. Now take the minimum difference of the adjacent elements. Do this for all the possible combination of elements from given array. From all the minimum differences of the sub arrays, print the maximum number. Input array: 1, 2, 5, 8 Input n: 3 Possible sub arrays and its minimum difference of adjacent elements: (1, 2, 5): 1 (1, 2, 8): 1 (1, 5, 8): 3 (2, 5, 8): 3 Ans: 3 So I could solve 1st one completely, we had to get to a formula and solution was of complexity O(1). Then for beautiful string problem, I spent more time solving. Still I got TLE on some cases. For the arrays problem I did not have much time, but I solved some of the test cases, and got TLE for the rest. I thought I won’t have a chance for the interview since I had only solved one question with all test cases and that too the easiest one. But I got a mail after about a week that I was selected for the interview and it will be held on 1st Feb,17 in the Bangalore campus. It was the IST week so I took permission from Professors of respective courses of which I’ll be missing the exam, HOD and TPO and finally reached Bangalore. Interview Round: It was a full day interview at the Bangalore campus starting from 10 am. Due to some circumstance I was late to reach the campus. All the students were already there and some had already given their 1st interview. I got to know that there will be 3 interviews (2 Tech + 1 HR). Also after some talk they told me that my name was already called earlier before I came. I was already nervous; this made me scared as I might have missed the opportunity. Some of the students were being taken for their 2nd interview. Finally there was official results announced for the 1st interviews and here I was, sitting there without the interview. After this when they were calling students for the next round, I asked whether my interview will be there or I missed. Ma’am realised my 1st interview was still remaining. And instead of one of the other who was going for 2nd interview I was given the chance. Finally 1st interview: (24 candidates) I was very nervous at that point of time. I think the interviewer might have noticed it, and he started with normal conversation, and told that I can go out anytime when I need a break. Finally he started with the standard question “Tell me about yourself” (which was asked in every interview). After this he asked me, “Tell me about the project that you are proud about”. I talked about a team project on which we had received a prize. Then there was conversation over the difficulties faced developing it and my contribution in the project. He gave me a problem based on tree. Print level order of the tree, such that each level is on its own line. A-> B, C B-> D C-> E, F Output: A B C D E F I gave a solution using BFS, a little modified to incorporate ‘each level on its own line’ using two queues. Then he asked for small modifications, e.g. in current solution there was extra space getting printed at the end. Then he modified tree, B-> D, A. Now, this was not a tree. So he told that if it’s not then don’t print the level order, instead print “It’s not a tree”. I thought of adding one attribute in node, traversed flag. First I just checked it on the go while making the level order, while explaining I realized that it will print the level order till the point where the node points backward in the tree is detected. So I modified to first check the tree and then print the level order. Then he told me not to add anything extra in the node. At this point I was trying to avoid hashing, and told that then for checking it will cost me more time. He then told me to think about alternative. So I told that hashing of node addresses is possible, but I am not aware of how to write the exact code for it. I explained the theory I knew and how it will help me, so he told me that just write hash wherever I am using it, and write what/how I am using it. At last, he told me that he was a product manager there and how many years he has worked. I was relaxed than before since interview went well. 2nd Interview: (~14 candidates) In this interview there were different questions unlike other, where there was one question and then follow up questions till the end. You are given a string as input and an integer ‘n’. You need to remove the nth consecutive letter from the given string. Input string: aaabbcd Input n: 2 Output: aabcd Then he told me to write a code for Sudoku solver. I asked him what must be the time complexity of the solution. He simply told me, ‘I did not ask for any time complexity’. So I gave a brute force solution which was easy to read and as small as I could make it. He liked the design of my resume so he asked me from where I got it. I told that I made it myself and have mentioned in it that I know how to use Photoshop. So he asked me why I want to pursue this job and not be a designer. And that’s it. 3rd Interview: (8 candidates) This was the most interesting interview I had. It started off with a simple data structure problem and ended in OS theory based on it. He asked me to make a recursive function to reverse a linked list. I told that I have already done it once. Be honest. After writing it down, since my function had void return type he told me that I should return something and reduce the number of arguments. I did that. Then he told me, to think that function as a black-box. (It means that I will only know what I need to give it as arguments and what it will return. I’ll know it will reverse the linked list, but won’t know the exact steps how it does that.) He told me to write a stub which will determine whether the function reverses the linked list in place or out of place. In place means that after calling the function the data remains in the same address location as it was before, out of place otherwise. First I told that I will only need to check one node whether it has the same address as before, because I thought either the function will make new nodes for all existing or it will do it using same nodes. But he told me it might not be this way. So I gave a solution using a stack which stored the address of all nodes. Here is where OS starts to come into picture. He asked me whether my function was thread-safe. Answer was no. So he asked me why not. I explained that during execution of the function it will have some pointers hanging, and not pointing to correct destination, if some other thread uses the linked list at this point it won’t get the proper data. He told me to make it thread safe. At first I kept only one flag. He asked me whether it was sufficient. It turned out that even that flag was not thread-safe. Finally I told that solution to that would be using a semaphore instead of the flag. He asked me what is the difference between the flag that I implemented and the semaphore I was talking about, also where is semaphore implemented. Then it ends with discussion on using semaphore for the solution. He then asked me to tell about an incident where I got stuck on some problem and then solved and improved the project from that. I told him about how I started to develop games, where my first target was to take input on console without blocking the execution. Then what I did for graphics, how it was stuttering and finally how I solved the stutter. Also during ‘Why Microsoft’ discussion I told that I had played the games like RoN, and like to play games. So he told me why not choose career on gaming rather than what I am trying to get there. That was it. I was done with all the 3 interviews. Finally after some waiting for other candidates to finish their last round, it was time for results. They selected 4 candidates and I was one of them. It was done by 5 pm. I was asked some standard questions in all the three interviews, like ‘Tell me about yourself’, ‘Why Microsoft’ or ‘Why not this that you do (design/game), and the job here’. Be prepared for such questions.
